clue.text: Crush on street making late news

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: to crush people is to oppress them

explanation.surface: Someone describes a stampede in the street that made the last-minute headlines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crush' looks like a crowd of people, but here it is a verb meaning to tyrannise; 'on' in an across clue puts it after the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Stop press is a newspaper column for stories that arrived after printing began.

clue.text: Old historian abandoning States — understood?

indicators.note: the historian abandons, i.e. loses, the letters for the States

parts.note: Tacitus was a Roman historian
US, the United States

explanation.surface: A query whether an ancient chronicler who left America was ever really grasped.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit agreement is implied or understood without being spoken.

clue.text: Stuck with former boss at the Telegraph?

parts.note: past means former, as in past times
a newspaper's boss is its editor, ED

explanation.surface: A pun on a former boss of this very newspaper being stuck in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pasted has been glued down, so it is stuck.

clue.text: Have no truck with junk

explanation.surface: Rejecting rubbish, with a nod to the lorry that might carry it.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb refuse means decline; the noun refuse, stressed differently, means rubbish.

clue.text: Make short work of cream puff for a start

parts.note: to cream off is to skim, taking the top layer

indicators.note: only the start, the opening letter, of puff is used

explanation.surface: A baker rushes through a cream puff to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to do something hurriedly or with too little effort or material.

clue.text: Incongruous representation of other map, possibly?

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: the word METAPHOR mixed up gives exactly the letters of other map

explanation.surface: A query whether a jumbled alternative chart might count as an odd image.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer itself is the wordplay, MIXED telling you to scramble METAPHOR into OTHER MAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed metaphor combines clashing images, an incongruous figure of speech.

clue.text: Domino effect of a car on thin ice skidding

indicators.note: a skidding car slides out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A car sliding on ice sets off a multi-vehicle pile-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain reaction is a series of events each triggering the next, like falling dominoes.

clue.text: Five-and-three, say, in old money?

parts.note: a five and a three are pieces that make up eight, and the answer is also an old Spanish coin

explanation.surface: Someone converting a sum into pre-decimal currency.
explanation.walkthrough: Five and three are two pieces of the number eight; the phrase is also the old Spanish silver dollar of pirate fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces of eight were Spanish dollars, a historic coinage beloved of pirate stories.

clue.text: You said cut up wood — it's prickly!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to crop is to cut short

indicators.note: spoken, you sounds like the letter U

parts.note: said aloud, the word you is the letter U
pine is a wood

explanation.surface: Someone chopped timber and found it spiky.
explanation.definitionFit: The porcupine is a rodent covered in sharp quills, the prickly animal par excellence.

clue.text: Raw items in hors d'oeuvres I introduced

indicators.note: the I is brought into the middle of the starters

parts.note: crudites are raw vegetable starters

explanation.surface: A host explains bringing out raw vegetable starters.
explanation.definitionFit: Crudities are crude or unripe things, raw in the sense of unrefined.

clue.text: No more time for public

parts.note: when something is no more, it is over

explanation.surface: Time is up for something open to all.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt actions are done openly, in public view.

clue.text: More important brother

definitions.meaning: ..., as in a ... claim that takes precedence
a monk ranking below an abbot

explanation.definitionFit: A prior claim outranks others; a prior is a senior monastic brother.

clue.text: Inches from hedge sparrow

indicators.note: the letters are taken out from within the two words

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher measures a dunnock in imperial units.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inches' looks like a noun of measurement, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge is to move gradually, a little at a time, as one inches forward.

clue.text: Welly-boot we regularly found in barge

indicators.note: every other letter is taken from the words, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Wellingtons turn up on a canal boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barge' looks like a boat, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow your way in is to barge, shoving through rudely.

clue.text: Bit of rice put in to achieve texture

indicators.note: the letter is put into the middle of the other word

parts.note: to gain something is to achieve it

indicators.note: a bit of the word, its first letter, is taken

explanation.surface: A cook adds a little rice to improve a dish's mouthfeel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of rice' looks like a definition of the answer itself, but supplies only R.
explanation.definitionFit: Grain is the texture of wood, stone or fabric, the pattern of its fibres.

clue.text: Mount Everest's two lowest sections require no name

indicators.note: in a down clue, the lowest letters are the last two
no name means the letter for name is dropped

parts.note: to need is to require

explanation.surface: A mountaineer is told the foothills of Everest need no naming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a mountain beside Everest, but it is a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A steed is a horse one rides, and a mount is a horse for riding.

clue.text: Force misrepresented policeman, Ian, falsely nicked

indicators.note: misrepresented means the letters are presented in a wrong order
falsely says the letters are jumbled; nicked says Ian's letters are taken away from the policeman

explanation.surface: An officer, misreported, wrongly arrested a man called Ian under duress.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of POLICEMAN minus those of IAN, rearranged, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel is to force someone to act, by pressure or authority.

clue.text: Told you so — old Penny's in debt

parts.note: there, as in 'There! Told you so!'
D, from Latin denarius, was the old British penny

explanation.surface: Someone gloats that a spendthrift's last coin has gone and they owe money.
explanation.walkthrough: D was the symbol for the pre-1971 British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the red means overdrawn, from red ink used for debts in ledgers.

clue.text: Support from British stock

parts.note: stock means lineage, a race of people

explanation.surface: Backing comes from British shares.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is a support or prop that holds something firm.

clue.text: Starchy type — awkward when hot!

definitions.meaning: an awkward issue nobody wants to hold

explanation.surface: A tuber that is tricky to handle straight from the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato is a starchy tuber; a hot potato is a controversial, awkward problem.

clue.text: Queen's tirade rambling

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: The monarch delivers a meandering outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means wandering or straying, as a rambling traveller does.

clue.text: Ecstasy taken by Rod lost its effect

indicators.note: the rod takes in the drug, holding it inside

parts.note: a wand is a thin rod
E is the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A man called Rod took a pill and it wore off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like a man's name but is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To wane is to diminish, as an effect fades away.

clue.text: Batty woman visiting Alaska in warm jacket

indicators.note: one visiting a place is inside it

parts.note: AK is the postal abbreviation for Alaska
Nora Batty is a character in Last of the Summer Wine

explanation.surface: A dotty lady heads to Alaska wearing a parka.
explanation.walkthrough: Nora Batty is the wrinkled-stockinged housewife of Last of the Summer Wine, a long-running British TV sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: An anorak is a hooded waterproof jacket, worn against cold.

clue.text: Occasion enhanced at the outset with Latin dancing

indicators.note: only the outset, the opening letter, of enhanced is used
dancing letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: An event livened up from the start by salsa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasion' looks like a noun but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to bring it about as a consequence, to occasion it.

clue.text: Quick shot acquiring prey — take note

indicators.note: the shot acquires the next piece, added on

parts.note: a nip is a small drink, a shot

indicators.note: take means remove the note from prey

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A hunter's fast shot brings down a quarry; write it down.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippy means quick and agile, as in a nippy little car.

clue.text: Indeed, service is long!

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes or indeed
RN, the Royal Navy, is an armed service

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a church service drags on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn for it, desire it deeply.

clue.text: Tax initially taken involving typist's hopeless error

indicators.note: the initial letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A levy imposed after a secretary's dreadful mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of produce or income paid as a tax to the church.

clue.text: Mark's mum leaving Australian possessions to the auditor

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so what remains is heard

parts.note: in Australia a swag of belongings is a matilda, as in Waltzing Matilda; mum (MA) leaving it gives TILDA

explanation.surface: A boy's mother departs the outback, taking her belongings to the accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' looks like an accountant but is a listener; what is left after dropping MA, TILDA, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilde is the wavy diacritical mark over a letter, as in Spanish ñ.

clue.text: With husband on a boat, I roll about in this form of transport

indicators.note: about means turned round, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seasick traveller rolls about on deck with their spouse, then wonders about flying.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot-air balloon is a craft lifted by heated air, a way of travelling.

clue.text: Not requiring special training, a Parisian's got rid of

parts.note: a Parisian says un for a, and the 's gives S
to kill is to get rid of

explanation.surface: A Frenchman did away with a job needing no expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: Unskilled work needs no special expertise or qualifications.
